yaml.title: Internal Data Exploration
yaml.subtitle: Browsing BMS data, differential expression, co-expression networks, multi-omics integration, pathway enrichment, and transcription factor analysis

markdown.markdown:
This chapter covers everything you can learn from BMS in-house data. It is organised into six layers, each building on the previous: ```{=html}
A
Data Browsing — what samples, clones, molecules, and timepoints are available
B
Differential Expression & Abundance (DEG/DAA) — which features change between high and low producers
C
Co-expression Networks (WGCNA) — which genes/proteins/metabolites move together
D
Multi-Omics Integration (MOFA) — latent factors that explain productivity variation across all omics layers simultaneously
E
Pathway & Functional Enrichment — KEGG and GO enrichment stored on the KG
F
Transcription Factor Analysis — master regulators of high-producer gene programs
``` --- ## A · Data Browsing {#sec-browsing} ::: {.query-box} What samples are available for the Nivo molecule in Study 1? ::: ::: {.query-box} Which days have both transcriptomics and proteomics measurements in Study 1? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show qP, titre, and IVCD values across all Nivo clones in Study 1. ::: Use the molecule filter to restrict any query to a single drug candidate (`Nivo` or `C144`). --- ## B · Differential Expression & Abundance {#sec-deg} ### What is DEG/DAA? **Differential Expression Analysis (DEG)** identifies genes whose mRNA levels differ significantly between two sample groups — in this KG, typically high vs. low producers. **Differential Abundance Analysis (DAA)** applies the same logic to proteins and metabolites. Results are stored as directed edges from each molecular feature to a Cohort node, with properties capturing the magnitude and significance of the difference. | Omics layer | Method | Covariate | Normalisation | |---|---|---|---| | Transcriptomics (DEG) | DESeq2 | Time | TPM | | Proteomics (DAA) | T-test | Time | Median central log₂ | | Metabolomics (DAA) | T-test | Time | Median central log₂ | ### Querying DEG/DAA Results ::: {.query-box} Which genes are upregulated in cohort Nivo_study1_all_high_vs_Nivo_study1_all_low with adj_pvalue < 0.05 and abs_log2fc > 2? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show genes downregulated in high vs. low C144 producers in Study 1, with abs_log2fc > 1.5. ::: ::: {.query-box} Which proteins are differentially abundant in high vs. low Nivo producers in Study 1? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show differentially abundant metabolites in the pellet fraction for high vs. low C144 producers. ::: ::: {.query-box} Which genes are consistently upregulated in at least 7 out of 10 high vs. low producer cohorts in Study 1? ::: **The multi-filter shortlisting funnel (Study 1):** | Filter step | Genes remaining | |---|---| | All DEGs across 232 cohorts | 11,481 | | adj_pvalue < 0.05 and abs_log2fc > 2 | 5,682 | | Directional consistency — RNA and protein both up or both down | 775 | | Upregulated in high producers | 330 | | Concordant RNA–protein regulation and Spearman r > 0.5 with qP | **63** | ### How to Interpret DEG/DAA Results | Output column | Source edge property | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `abs_log2fc` | `upregulated.abs_log2fc` | Absolute log₂ fold-change (cohort A vs. B). Higher = larger difference. | | `direction` | `upregulated.direction` | `positive` = higher in cohort A (high producers); `negative` = higher in cohort B | | `adj_pvalue` | `upregulated.adj_pvalue` | BH-corrected p-value. Use < 0.05 as significance threshold. | | `pvalue` | `upregulated.pvalue` | Nominal p-value. Prefer adj_pvalue for filtering. | | `sampling_type` | Metabolomics edges only | `pellet` = intracellular; `supernatant` = extracellular fraction | ::: {.callout-tip} For robust targets, filter for genes with consistent direction in ≥7/10 high-vs-low cohorts AND both RNA and protein showing the same directional change. The 63-gene shortlist above is a reliable starting point. ::: --- ## C · Co-expression Networks (WGCNA) {#sec-wgcna} ### What is WGCNA? **Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA)** groups genes, proteins, or metabolites that vary together across samples into **modules**. Each module is summarised by its **Module Eigengene (ME)** — the first principal component of all members — which is then correlated with bioprocess traits (qP, titre, IVCD) to identify productivity-associated modules. The pipeline runs in five steps: ```{=html}
1
Correlate — pairwise feature-to-feature correlations across 36 samples × 3 omics layers
2
Weight — raise to soft-threshold power β to amplify strong connections and suppress noise (β = 19 genes, 6 protein, 14 metabolites)
3
Cluster — build Topological Overlap Matrix (TOM) → hierarchical clustering → modules (20 gene, 5 protein, 5 metabolite)
4
Summarise — reduce each module to its Module Eigengene (1 value per sample)
5
Correlate to traits — Pearson r of each ME vs. qP, titre, IVCD → significant modules flagged
``` > **Published precedent:** Melville et al. (2011, *Journal of Biotechnology*) applied WGCNA to 295 microarrays from 121 CHO cultures and identified six transcriptional modules correlated with qP, growth rate, and viability — directly validating this approach for CHO productivity analysis. In the KG, modules are stored as **Network nodes** (e.g., `network_2_gene`, `network_1_protein`). Module membership is stored on `gene_part_of`, `protein_part_of`, and `metabolite_part_of` edges. ### Querying WGCNA Results ::: {.query-box} Which gene WGCNA networks (modules) are positively correlated with qP in Study 1? ::: ::: {.query-box} List all genes in network_2_gene (WGCNA module M1) with their network_membership (kME) scores, sorted descending. ::: ::: {.query-box} What are the top 10 hub genes (is_hub = true) in network_2_gene? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show genes in network_2_gene with gs_qp > 0.5, ranked by descending network_membership. ::: ::: {.query-box} Which protein WGCNA modules correlate with IVCD in Study 1? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show metabolite module members with significant correlation to qP, ranked by gs_qp. ::: ### How to Interpret WGCNA Results | Output column | Source edge property | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `network_membership` | `gene_part_of.network_membership` | kME — how strongly a gene tracks its module eigengene (0–1; closer to 1 = stronger hub) | | `gs_qp` | `gene_part_of.gs_qp` | Gene significance for qP — Pearson r of gene expression with qP across samples | | `gs_ivcd` | `gene_part_of.gs_ivcd` | Gene significance for IVCD | | `gs_titre` | `gene_part_of.gs_titre` | Gene significance for product titre | | `gs_qp_pval` | `gene_part_of.gs_qp_pval` | P-value for gs_qp — use < 0.05 for significance | | `sig_qp` / `sig_ivcd` / `sig_titre` | Boolean flags | `true` = gene–trait association is statistically significant | | `is_hub` | `gene_part_of.is_hub` | `true` = high intramodular connectivity; hub gene | | `pearson_correlation` | `gene_network_correlated_with_phenotype` | Module eigengene vs. phenotype Pearson r | | `fdr` | Same edge | BH-corrected FDR for module–phenotype correlation | ::: {.callout-note} **Key modules identified in Study 1:** - `network_2_gene` (M1 Pro-productivity) — ER processing / UPR enriched. ME positively correlated with qP. - `network_18_gene` (M18 Anti-productivity) — Cell cycle / DNA replication enriched. ME negatively correlated with qP. ::: --- ## D · Multi-Omics Factor Analysis (MOFA) {#sec-mofa} ### What is MOFA? **Multi-Omics Factor Analysis (MOFA)** is an unsupervised dimensionality-reduction method that integrates transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics simultaneously to identify **latent factors** — hidden biological programs that explain variation across samples. Each factor is a weighted linear combination of features across all three omics layers. Features with large weights drive that factor; the factor score for each sample reflects how strongly the sample expresses that biological program. ```{=html}
1
Input preparation — top 5,000 variable features (transcriptomics & proteomics), all 596 metabolite features
2
MOFA decomposition — joint matrix factorisation across 3 omics views; K = 10 latent factors
3
Factor–trait correlation — Spearman's ρ of each factor score vs. qP, titre, IVCD across 36 samples
4
Feature weight interpretation — top 80th percentile features per factor per layer extracted for pathway enrichment
``` **Significant factors and their biological meaning:** | Factor | Correlation pattern | Interpretation | |---|---|---| | **Factor 1** | qP +0.848 · IVCD +0.860 · Titre +0.904 | Full-spectrum productivity signal — the most actionable factor | | Factor 2 | qP positive · IVCD negative | High efficiency per cell; not driven by biomass accumulation | | Factor 3 | Proteomics-only | Post-translational regulatory axis decoupled from transcription | | Factor 4 | Transcriptomics-only | Transcriptional program not yet reflected in protein or metabolite levels | | Factor 5 | Titre and qP strongly negative | Pure metabolic suppressor acting on secretory machinery | ### Querying MOFA Results ::: {.query-box} Which genes have the highest positive MOFA Factor 1 weight in Study 1? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show proteins with MOFA Factor 1 weight above 0.3. ::: ::: {.query-box} Which metabolites contribute most to Factor 5? What pathways are enriched in those metabolites? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show per-sample MOFA Factor 1 scores for all Study 1 Nivo samples and overlay with qP values. ::: ::: {.query-box} Show genes that are consistently upregulated in high producers (≥7/10 cohorts), members of a pro-productivity WGCNA network, AND have positive MOFA Factor 1 weight. This is the triple-overlap pro-productivity shortlist. ::: ### How to Interpret MOFA Results | Output column | Source edge property | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `mofa_weight` | `gene_contributes_to_factor.mofa_weight` | MOFA loading weight. Positive = co-varies positively with factor; negative = inversely. Typical range: −1 to +1. | | `entity_type` | Same edge | `gene`, `protein`, or `metabolite` — which omics layer this feature belongs to | | `correlation` | `factor_correlated_with_phenotype.correlation` | Spearman ρ between factor scores and phenotype values across samples | | `direction` | Same edge | `positive` / `negative` — whether high factor scores associate with high or low phenotype | | `mofa_score` | `has_mofa_score.mofa_score` | Per-sample factor loading score (typically −5 to +5) | ::: {.callout-important} **Factor 1 is the most actionable.** Genes with high positive Factor 1 weights are pro-productivity candidates for overexpression. Genes with high negative weights are anti-productivity candidates for knockout. ::: --- ## E · Pathway & Functional Enrichment {#sec-pathways} ### What is Pathway Enrichment? Pathway enrichment analysis tests whether a set of genes or metabolites contains more members of a given biological pathway than expected by chance. Results are **pre-computed and stored in the KG** as edges from pathway nodes to cohort, network, or factor nodes — you query the results, not run the analysis. | Method | Input | What it detects | |---|---|---| | **GSEA** (Gene Set Enrichment Analysis) | Ranked gene list (by log2FC or MOFA weight) | Coordinated shifts across the full ranked list | | **ORA** (Over-Representation Analysis) | Binary DEG or module member list | Pathways with more hits than expected by chance | Both are applied to DEG cohorts, WGCNA modules, and MOFA factors. Databases: **KEGG Pathways** and **Gene Ontology** (BP, MF, CC). ### Querying Pathway Enrichment **On DEG cohorts:** ::: {.query-box} Which KEGG pathways are enriched (GSEA) in cohort Nivo_study1_all_high_vs_Nivo_study1_all_low? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show GO Biological Process terms enriched in downregulated genes of C144 high vs. low producers. ::: **On WGCNA modules:** ::: {.query-box} What KEGG pathways are enriched in gene network network_2_gene? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show GO terms enriched in the anti-productivity gene network network_18_gene. ::: **On MOFA factors:** ::: {.query-box} Which pathways are enriched in the top-weighted genes for MOFA Factor 1? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show KEGG pathway enrichment for MOFA Factor 5, separating positive and negative weight metabolites. ::: **Cross-molecule comparison:** ::: {.query-box} Compare enriched KEGG pathways between Nivo and C144 high vs. low producer cohorts. Which are shared and which are molecule-specific? ::: ### How to Interpret Enrichment Results | Output column | Source edge property | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `enrichment_score` | `kegg_pathway_enriched_in.enrichment_score` | NES for GSEA; fold-enrichment for ORA. Positive = enriched in upregulated / positive-weight genes. | | `padj` | Same edge | BH-corrected p-value. Use < 0.05. | | `overlap` | Same edge | Fraction of pathway genes in the input set. Higher = more pathway coverage. | | `analysis_type` | Same edge | `GSEA`, `ORA_upregulated`, `ORA_downregulated`, `ORA_Negative` | | `lead_genes` | Same edge | Gene symbols driving the enrichment signal (GSEA leading edge or ORA hits) | | `sampling_type` | Metabolomics edges only | `pellet` (intracellular) or `supernatant` (extracellular) | | `source_database` | `go_term_enriched_in` | `GO_BP`, `GO_MF`, or `GO_CC` | ### KEGG Metabolic Network Traversal The KG also stores the full KEGG metabolic network, enabling mechanistic gene-to-reaction queries: ::: {.query-box} Which KEGG pathway does gene LDHA belong to? ::: ::: {.query-box} Find all genes in the glycolysis KEGG pathway that are differentially expressed in high vs. low Nivo producers. ::: ::: {.query-box} Trace LDHA to its enzymatic activity and the metabolic reactions it catalyses. ::: --- ## F · Transcription Factor Analysis {#sec-tf} ### What is TF Enrichment? Transcription factor (TF) enrichment identifies upstream regulators whose target genes are over-represented in a DEG set or WGCNA module. It answers: *which TFs are driving the gene expression changes we observe in high producers?* The analysis uses **gseapy (enrich)** against the **ChEA 2022** database of curated TF–target relationships (from ChIP-seq experiments). Results are stored as edges from TF Gene nodes to Cohort or Network nodes. | Edge type | Meaning | |---|---| | `tf_regulates_cohort_degs` | TF whose targets are enriched in a cohort's DEG set | | `tf_regulates_network_genes` | TF whose targets are enriched in a WGCNA module's gene set | Available for: **Study 1 cohorts** and **WGCNA gene modules**. ### Querying TF Results ::: {.query-box} Which transcription factors regulate genes upregulated in cohort Nivo_study1_all_high_vs_Nivo_study1_all_low? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show TFs with padj < 0.01 whose targets are enriched among upregulated DEGs in C144 high producers. ::: ::: {.query-box} Which TFs regulate genes in pro-productivity WGCNA network network_2_gene? ::: ::: {.query-box} What TFs control the anti-productivity gene network network_18_gene? ::: ::: {.query-box} Trace gene HSPA5 upstream: what transcription factors regulate it in high-producer cohorts? ::: ::: {.query-box} Which TFs have the broadest target gene scope across all pro-productivity cohorts in Study 1? Identify master regulators. ::: ### How to Interpret TF Results | Output column | Source edge property | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `tf_symbol` | `tf_regulates_cohort_degs.tf_symbol` | Standardised gene symbol of the TF (e.g., `E2F4`, `NFE2L2`) | | `direction` | Same edge | `UP` = TF targets enriched in upregulated DEGs; `DOWN` = in downregulated DEGs | | `padj` | Same edge | BH-corrected p-value for TF enrichment significance | | `overlap` | Same edge | Fraction of TF targets in the DEG set | | `target_genes` | Same edge | Semicolon-delimited list of TF target gene symbols in the overlap | | `tf_term_original` | Same edge | Full ChEA term (e.g., `E2F4 20460467 ChIP-Seq MCF7 Human`) — shows source organism and assay | | `tf_database` | Same edge | Always `ChEA_2022` in this KG | **Key master regulators identified in Study 1:** | TF | Module association | padj | Biological role | |---|---|---|---| | **E2F4** | Anti-productivity (network_18_gene) | 3.7×10⁻¹²² | Cell cycle / DNA replication master regulator | | FOXM1 | Anti-productivity | Significant | Mitotic transcription factor | | E2F1 | Anti-productivity | Significant | Cell cycle entry | | MYC | Anti-productivity | Significant | Broad proliferation driver | | NFE2L2 (NRF2) | Pro-productivity (network_2_gene) | Significant | Oxidative stress / UPR response | | FOXO1 | Pro-productivity | Significant | Metabolism and stress resistance | | PPARA | Pro-productivity | Significant | Lipid metabolism and ER function | | SMARCA4 | Pro-productivity | Significant | Chromatin remodelling | ::: {.query-box} Is NFE2L2 itself differentially expressed in Nivo high vs. low producers in Study 1? ::: ::: {.query-box} Does E2F4 have a significant MOFA Factor 1 weight? :::

Positive = enriched in upregulated / positive-weight genes. | | `padj` | Same edge | BH-corrected p-value. Use < 0.05. | | `overlap` | Same edge | Fraction of pathway genes in the input set. Higher = more pathway coverage. | | `analysis_type` | Same edge | `GSEA`, `ORA_upregulated`, `ORA_downregulated`, `ORA_Negative` | | `lead_genes` | Same edge | Gene symbols driving the enrichment signal (GSEA leading edge or ORA hits) | | `sampling_type` | Metabolomics edges only | `pellet` (intracellular) or `supernatant` (extracellular) | | `source_database` | `go_term_enriched_in` | `GO_BP`, `GO_MF`, or `GO_CC` | ### KEGG Metabolic Network Traversal The KG also stores the full KEGG metabolic network, enabling mechanistic gene-to-reaction queries: ::: {.query-box} Which KEGG pathway does gene LDHA belong to? ::: ::: {.query-box} Find all genes in the glycolysis KEGG pathway that are differentially expressed in high vs. low Nivo producers. ::: ::: {.query-box} Trace LDHA to its enzymatic activity and the metabolic reactions it catalyses. ::: --- ## F · Transcription Factor Analysis {#sec-tf} ### What is TF Enrichment? Transcription factor (TF) enrichment identifies upstream regulators whose target genes are over-represented in a DEG set or WGCNA module. It answers: *which TFs are driving the gene expression changes we observe in high producers?* The analysis uses **gseapy (enrich)** against the **ChEA 2022** database of curated TF–target relationships (from ChIP-seq experiments). Results are stored as edges from TF Gene nodes to Cohort or Network nodes. | Edge type | Meaning | |---|---| | `tf_regulates_cohort_degs` | TF whose targets are enriched in a cohort's DEG set | | `tf_regulates_network_genes` | TF whose targets are enriched in a WGCNA module's gene set | Available for: **Study 1 cohorts** and **WGCNA gene modules**. ### Querying TF Results ::: {.query-box} Which transcription factors regulate genes upregulated in cohort Nivo_study1_all_high_vs_Nivo_study1_all_low? ::: ::: {.query-box} Show TFs with padj < 0.01 whose targets are enriched among upregulated DEGs in C144 high producers. ::: ::: {.query-box} Which TFs regulate genes in pro-productivity WGCNA network network_2_gene? ::: ::: {.query-box} What TFs control the anti-productivity gene network network_18_gene? ::: ::: {.query-box} Trace gene HSPA5 upstream: what transcription factors regulate it in high-producer cohorts? ::: ::: {.query-box} Which TFs have the broadest target gene scope across all pro-productivity cohorts in Study 1? Identify master regulators. ::: ### How to Interpret TF Results | Output column | Source edge property | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `tf_symbol` | `tf_regulates_cohort_degs.tf_symbol` | Standardised gene symbol of the TF (e.g., `E2F4`, `NFE2L2`) | | `direction` | Same edge | `UP` = TF targets enriched in upregulated DEGs; `DOWN` = in downregulated DEGs | | `padj` | Same edge | BH-corrected p-value for TF enrichment significance | | `overlap` | Same edge | Fraction of TF targets in the DEG set | | `target_genes` | Same edge | Semicolon-delimited list of TF target gene symbols in the overlap | | `tf_term_original` | Same edge | Full ChEA term (e.g., `E2F4 20460467 ChIP-Seq MCF7 Human`) — shows source organism and assay | | `tf_database` | Same edge | Always `ChEA_2022` in this KG | **Key master regulators identified in Study 1:** | TF | Module association | padj | Biological role | |---|---|---|---| | **E2F4** | Anti-productivity (network_18_gene) | 3.7×10⁻¹²² | Cell cycle / DNA replication master regulator | | FOXM1 | Anti-productivity | Significant | Mitotic transcription factor | | E2F1 | Anti-productivity | Significant | Cell cycle entry | | MYC | Anti-productivity | Significant | Broad proliferation driver | | NFE2L2 (NRF2) | Pro-productivity (network_2_gene) | Significant | Oxidative stress / UPR response | | FOXO1 | Pro-productivity | Significant | Metabolism and stress resistance | | PPARA | Pro-productivity | Significant | Lipid metabolism and ER function | | SMARCA4 | Pro-productivity | Significant | Chromatin remodelling | ::: {.query-box} Is NFE2L2 itself differentially expressed in Nivo high vs. low producers in Study 1? ::: ::: {.query-box} Does E2F4 have a significant MOFA Factor 1 weight? :::
